question: Does the isolated-triple versus same-passage-context effect hold on open-answer, general-domain multi-hop benchmarks rather than synthetic biomedical multiple-choice QA?
description: The only evidence that context-augmented training helps comes from two synthetic biomedical disease KGs with multiple-choice items (arxiv:2609.12230), and its own limitations section says broader validation is needed. The standard multi-hop benchmarks that the original research question names (MetaQA 1/2/3-hop with Hits@1, WebQSP/CWQ, 2WikiMultiHopQA or MoreHopQA with EM/F1 and gold evidence paths) are Freebase- or Wikipedia-based and use open answers, so nobody has tested whether the KG-grounded vs CG-grounded contrast survives there. Doing so requires solving the passage-provenance problem for those KGs as well.
rationale: External validity is the difference between reporting a domain-specific effect and a general finding about KgQA training, and the benchmark and metric choices needed to test it are already identified in the investigation plan.
